messages:
anya: Thanks everyone for the great questions during the all-hands. Posting a live follow-up thread with clarifications on travel, offsites, and workspace stuff. Will update as we get more Qs.

lucy: quick one — is there a new cap on airfare for FY26 offsites?

michelle: Short answer: yes, we set a guideline band to keep budgets predictable. Economy for flights <6h, premium economy okay for 6–10h with manager OK, and >10h we may approve one upgrade on a case-by-case basis.

matt: who approves the 10h exceptions?

michelle: Manager + People Ops signoff. If it's exec-level travel, add your director. Use the travel approval form (link coming).

devin: Concur or manual? We've had issues with reimbursements taking forever.

travel-bot: Reminder: All bookings should go through Concur for company-paid travel. Unapproved bookings are reimbursed at the lowest allowed fare band.

anya: Reimbursement timeline: finance aims for 7 business days after a complete expense report. Missing receipts or incorrect GL codes delay it. If stuck, ping @finance-ops.

jamal: On international travel — company will provide visa invitation letters and cover visa fees when travel is required by the company or for client work. For optional conference attendance, check with your manager first.

lucy: For offsites, will there be per-diem or meal reimbursement?

michelle: Offsites prioritized by team: daily meal stipend set at $60/day while traveling for overnight offsite. Team dinners above $60 should have pre-approval if expecting to exceed budget. Keep receipts.

devin: Any childcare or family travel support? We asked at the all-hands.

anya: We have a caregiving stipend pilot for this year. If caregiving costs are a barrier to attending required company events, People Ops can approve a one-time stipend — mention it on the travel approval form and we'll route for review.

matt: Hotel preferences? We had a lot of confusion last time about which hotels were 'preferred'.

michelle: We'll publish a list of preferred hotels per city in the offsite playbook. Preferred = negotiated rates + easy invoice. If you book outside those, expect manager approval and use company card where possible.

lucy: What about climate or accessibility needs?

anya: Always indicate accessibility or dietary needs on the form. We'll coordinate accommodations and meals. For larger offsites we publish a dietary/allergy form in the event RSVP.

devin: Are team socials on the last night covered? Some folks had surprise charges for alcohol before.

michelle: Alcohol is allowed for team dinners but must be reasonable and within spend guidelines. If team expects heavy alcohol spend, get pre-approval and classify as a special event expense.

jamal: For hybrid workers: desk hoteling and satellite days — any policy changes?

anya: No sweeping changes. Desk reservations will open 10 days before your intended office day. Satellite office days (monthly) are supported; teams are encouraged to coordinate a week in advance. If you need guaranteed desk plus meeting rooms, request via the office portal and tag @people-ops.

matt: If someone is remote and needs to travel for client work, do they book airfare + hotel using company card?

travel-bot: Yes — client work = company-paid. Use Concur and company card. If you don't have a company card, submit a request and we'll provision one for frequent travelers.

lucy: Expense codes — any change? Last time our invoices got tagged wrong.

anya: Use project code prefix "OFF-" for offsite expenses. We'll add examples to the playbook. Finance will run a reconciliation and DEV leads will get a report.

devin: Can we get a short office-hours drop-in with People Ops to walk through Concur + approvals?

anya: Good idea — scheduling 2x office-hours next week (Tue/Thu 11–12 PT). I'll post a calendar invite and a recording.

michelle: Also — offsite code of conduct reminder: professional behavior expected, respect everyone's boundaries. We'll circulate the short CoC and include reporting contacts.

matt: Is there a carbon offset option when booking? some folks asked at all-hands.

jamal: We're piloting carbon offsets for company-paid flights this quarter. It auto-adds a small fee to bookings — opt-out is allowed but please discuss with manager if you do.

lucy: One last Q — who covers unexpected travel quarantine or testing for international travel?

anya: If the travel is company-directed, we cover mandatory testing/quarantine costs. If you choose to extend personal travel, those costs are personal.

anya: I'll update the offsite/travel playbook doc and paste the link here when it's live. Keep posting questions here and we'll fold them into the FAQ. Thanks! :raised_hands:
